# A10 — Legacy Tracked Requirements — Screen Spec Audit Record

**Process note**: A10 was never generated by the original Claude Design package (the one real gap
in the 24-screen set, see `docs/frontend/prototype-screen-specs/README.md`). Written from scratch
this session, applying SLF-01 through SLF-05's already-converged dispositions directly during
authorship (not as a naive first draft later corrected) — grounded in the real backend
(`src/modules/subject/domain/requirement-assignment.ts`,
`src/modules/subject/application/{requirement-service,document-request-service}.ts`,
`src/modules/identity/domain/authorization.ts`), not just the plan's one-paragraph A10 summary. One
BLIND Codex pass (`codex exec --skip-git-repo-check`, prompt/output archived at
`C:\Users\Usuario\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\...\scratchpad\codex-a10-prompt.txt` /
`codex-a10-output.txt` for this session) + one Claude reconciliation round, same deliberate scope
reduction as every other screen in this project.

**Reconciliation**: Codex's blind read (no visibility into this record, no visibility into the
other 24 screens' scores) landed at Functional 94.0 / Visual 87.0 / Consolidated 91.2 — the first
screen in this entire project to clear the Baseline Pass floor on a first pass (all 24 others scored
25.4–50.2 pre-revision). Claude's own independent read, done before seeing Codex's output, converged
on the same overall shape: strong RBAC/route/traceability coverage (grounded directly in
`authorization.ts`, not inferred), a genuine V7 thesis (frozen manual snapshot vs. live independent
timeline, derived from the real fact that `createDocumentRequest` never touches
`RequirementAssignment.status`), but incomplete interactive-state coverage (hover/focus/pressed/
loading/disabled/read-only never enumerated), thin typography-role naming, no post-mutation
toast/feedback per action, and an unoperationalized "activity-recency" ordering claim (no tie-break
rule). Codex's specific findings are adopted as-is — well-evidenced, consistent with the kind of gap
found on A09/A11/A14 even after their own revisions. Applied a direct revision closing every Major
and Moderate finding (see "Required revision — applied" below) before finalizing this record, per
the task's instruction to land as close to the other 24's post-revision bar as possible on the first
real pass, not to ship a first draft. Final scores below reflect the POST-revision spec now on disk.

Findings:
- Critical: none.
- Major (all resolved in this session's revision — see below): interactive-state coverage
  (hover/focus/pressed/loading/disabled/read-only) was unspecified pre-revision; typography roles
  were named only partially; no per-action success/error feedback was specified.
- Moderate (all resolved): "activity recency" ordering was asserted but not operationalized (no
  sort key, no tie-break, no behavior on live reorder); no accessible live-region behavior for
  timeline entries arriving out of band.
- Minor: the frozen-snapshot/live-timeline pattern (SYSTEM EVOLUTION CANDIDATE below) has only this
  one instance in the current 25-screen set — cannot yet be scored as a reused cross-screen
  vocabulary (V7's 1-point deduction, V8 unaffected since no contradiction exists, only absence of
  reuse opportunity).

Design-system dispositions:
- SPEC GAP: none remaining after this session's revision (interactive states, typography roles,
  per-action feedback, ordering rule, live-region announcement, version/date line all added).
- SYSTEM GAP: whether a normative "emphasized StatusBadge" size variant and a normative
  static-surface-vs-live-region pairing exist — flagged for the design-system maintainer to confirm
  (same remediation owner as SLF-01/02, not a new independent finding since no 3rd screen shares
  this specific need yet).
- SYSTEM CONSTRAINT: none.
- JUSTIFIED EXCEPTION: `CANCELLED` chasing occurrences omitted from the timeline entirely (an event
  that stopped happening is not a historical event to display); the empty-state CTA points to A11
  rather than to creating a new legacy link, reinforcing the "mechanism winding down" thesis even
  with zero data — both local, deliberate, not candidates for a system rule.
- SYSTEM EVOLUTION CANDIDATE: the "epistemic snapshot + live operational timeline" pattern (a manual
  status frozen at the moment of last human action, paired with an always-current event log
  explicitly labeled as unsynchronized with that snapshot) is a plausible reusable pattern for any
  future screen with the same shape (a manually-set status that async processes never rewrite) — not
  yet promoted, since this is its first and only instance.

Required revision — applied in this session (before finalizing this record):
- Added a compact interactive-state matrix (hover/focus-visible/pressed-via-loading/disabled/
  read-only) for table rows, links, and action buttons, including the idempotency/single-flight
  discipline already established for A14's "Gerar agora."
- Added a per-action post-mutation feedback subsection (link/unlink, request, revoke, edit, delete)
  naming the exact Toast/InlineNotice per success and failure path.
- Added a typography-roles subsection (V2) naming semantic roles for vínculo name, notes, timestamps,
  recipient email, and file name, including explicit wrapping/truncation rules for PT-BR realistic
  data (long emails/filenames use `word-break`, never mid-string truncation, inside the expanded
  timeline).
- Operationalized the "activity recency" ordering claim into a concrete 4-tier sort key with a
  tie-break rule and a no-reflow-mid-read guarantee.
- Added an `aria-live="polite"` behavior for timeline entries arriving out of band (distinct from
  the toast-based announcement for user-triggered mutations).
- Added the version/date line at the top of the spec.

Rendered-review checks to defer to the later gate:
- Whether the frozen-snapshot vs. live-timeline visual contrast reads as "different kind of
  information," not "the snapshot looks broken/disabled," once rendered with real tokens.
- Optical balance of the nested submission-under-request indentation at realistic timeline lengths
  (many requests, several submissions each).
- Contrast of the neutral/warning/critical badges and the snapshot's stronger bottom border in situ.
- Legibility of long PT-BR vendor names, emails, and filenames in the actual chosen font at the
  specified sizes.
- Whether the 180ms fade-in for new timeline entries is perceptible without being distracting.
- Desktop table and mobile card behavior at high row counts with mixed RBAC-driven action-menu
